Still deciding whether the Chartered Pathway is right for you? Here are the questions professionals and employers ask most often before applying.
Eligible levy-funded employers & eligible apprentices aged 16–24
It can be — depending on your employer and eligibility.
Levy-paying employers — eligible apprenticeship training can be funded through available employer levy funds.
Eligible apprentices aged 16–24 — eligible apprenticeship training can be funded at 100%, subject to the applicable apprenticeship funding rules.
For eligible non-levy apprentices aged 25+, government funding may cover 95%, with the employer contributing the remaining 5%.
Will I personally have to pay for the apprenticeship?
No eligible apprenticeship training cost is charged to the learner.
The apprentice must not be charged for eligible apprenticeship training or assessment costs.
The exact employer funding arrangement is confirmed before enrolment.

No. ChPP is awarded independently by APM.

The specialists behind the Chartered Pathway

Former Chairman of the Association for Project Management (APM), Steve Wake led the Association during its progression to Chartered status. He founded APM's EVM and Planning, Monitoring & Control groups, led the development of BS 202001 Project Controls, and continues to contribute to UK and international Project Controls standards.

Chief Examiner for APMG's Managing Benefits and Managing Portfolios certifications, Stephen Jenner is a leading specialist in project portfolio and benefits realisation management. His background includes senior UK Civil Service leadership, cross-government benefits management and extensive international work in portfolio strategy and professional development.

Ray Mead is the owner and director of p3m global, a specialist portfolio, programme and project management consultancy. He is co-author of Delivering Successful PMOs, drawing on practical experience in designing and implementing enterprise PMOs and developing organisational project-management capability internationally.
